account: It is early morning on day 1. I have read and returned the updated appointment book. Today I am due at the office at 08:00, the mill for a grain inspection at 10:00, home for lunch, the office for council letters at 13:00, my neighbour's dockside cottage for tea at 15:00, the office at 16:30, and the great hall at 18:00 for the builder's lighting and table inspection, which I approved yesterday. The secretary confirmed that inspection was entered and intended to notify the builder and speak with Freight. What seems unusual is Freight's remark just now: both entrances are closed, an open shutter at (-46, -59, 31) should also be checked, and everything will be kept quiet until eighteen. I heard this from nearby but did not see whom Freight was addressing or which entrances he meant. The secretary is beside me. Yesterday I also saw a plank placed in the hall area at (-58, -60, 26). These may be preparations for the inspection, perhaps involving lighting and keeping the room enclosed, but I do not yet know why quiet or closed shutters are needed. I should not assume a hidden purpose without asking. Separately, yesterday evening I heard the innkeeper seeking my neighbour about returning an unused lantern payment; I do not know whether that is connected.
